findings.description: storage_encrypted is set to false, so the RDS MySQL instance and its snapshots store all data unencrypted on disk.

publicly_accessible = true gives the RDS instance a public endpoint, exposing the MySQL listener to the internet if the subnet routes to an internet gateway, leaving only a security-group rule as protection for an unencrypted database with an 'admin' master user.

The attached parameter group does not set require_secure_transport = ON and the PHP client uses mysqli_connect without TLS options, so credentials and query data can traverse the network in cleartext.
The master username is hard-coded to "admin", a well-known default that assists credential-guessing attacks against the publicly reachable endpoint.

The RDS master username and var.password are interpolated into the instance user_data script, which is stored unencrypted and retrievable in cleartext from the instance metadata service (and Terraform state) by any process or attacker reaching the instance.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is set, so the root volume holding the plaintext dbinfo.inc credentials file is unencrypted at rest.

No metadata_options block enforcing http_tokens = "required" is present, so IMDSv1 remains enabled; combined with the wildcard instance profile and a PHP application, SSRF could be used to exfiltrate role credentials.

The bootstrap script installs httpd serving the form application over plain HTTP with no TLS configuration, so submitted personal data (NAME, ADDRESS) travels in cleartext; the public_dns output indicates it is intended to be reached externally.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*" to the role attached to the web server; compromise of the instance yields near-total control of S3, EC2 and RDS in the account, including privilege escalation via ec2:RunInstances with iam:PassRole-equivalent instance profile abuse and rds:RestoreDBInstanceFromDBSnapshot.
The database security group permits all protocols and ports outbound to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unconstrained path for data exfiltration or callback traffic from the data tier.
Port 3306 is opened to the whole VPC CIDR instead of being sourced from the application instance's security group, so any workload in the VPC can reach the database directly.

The database security group and the db subnet group place the publicly_accessible RDS instance in the same subnets (portal_subnet_a/b) used by the public-facing application server, so there is no network segmentation between the internet-facing web tier and the data tier.
The database endpoint of a publicly accessible instance is emitted as an unmarked Terraform output, disclosing the target host to anyone with access to state or CI logs.
